notes:
User is considering a fall sprint triathlon and wants help tracking progress and developing a practical training plan. Current fitness:
- Does mixed cardio and strength training at the gym.
- Plays volleyball on weeknights; team is the “Net Ninjas,” currently 5–2. Plays soccer Sundays.
- Can swim laps, but pace is slow; swimming is the primary triathlon focus.
- Limited running experience; recent 5K in 32:15.
- Does not own a bike yet, plans to buy one soon, and wants to improve cycling.
- Wants training prioritized around sports commitments.
- Proposed structure: 2–3 swims, 2 bike sessions, 1–2 runs, occasional bricks, and 1 strength session, adjusted around volleyball/soccer. Sample: Tuesday swim, Wednesday longer ride, Friday easy run, Saturday bike/interval or occasional bike-to-run brick, Monday/Thursday volleyball, Sunday soccer.
- Mobility/flexibility work 1–2 times weekly may support swimming, cycling, running, and injury prevention, especially with volleyball/soccer.
- Interested in a professional bike fitting for comfort, efficiency, and injury prevention. No local shops suggested because location is unknown; if asked, request city/state or region and prioritize an experienced/certified fitter, ideally with triathlon experience, over brand.

User is also organizing a recreational office basketball league:
- Plans to begin with an interest survey.
- Considering group clinics and online resources for beginners; later may add one-on-one coaching, practice sessions, or skill divisions.
- Considering modest prizes/recognition, while keeping the league fun, inclusive, and focused on camaraderie rather than competition.
- Previously agreed to find a co-organizer, scale back responsibilities, and schedule games around training/rest to avoid burnout/injury.
- Plans a season-ending mini tournament and may invite volleyball-league friends. Considering mixed teams versus separate teams; a hybrid approach—mixed teams for some round-robin/social games, then original teams for finals—could balance new connections with team chemistry. Surveying participants is advisable.
